e: The FBI announces that North Korea used fake video calls to steal $400 million in cryptocurrency.
The International Criminal Court closes its investigations into suspected war crimes committed by US troops in Afghanistan, following institutional sanctions imposed by the US on the court.
The FAA issues a nationwide ground stop for the first time since 9/11, due to a "telecommunications outage".
Jensen Huang resigns as the CEO of Nvidia, following revelations of two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China.
One person is killed and four are injured in a gun attack at and outside a fitness center in downtown Washington, D.C.
A three-story apartment building collapses in Brooklyn, New York City, killing eight people and injuring 17 others.
A car crashes into a food stand near a bus stop in the North Hollywood section of Los Angeles, killing three people and seriously injuring three more.

Democrat Scott Colom defeats incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi Senate election, becoming the state's first black U.S. senator since 1874 and the first Democrat elected to the seat since 1982.
The United States Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth awards medal to war memorial guard.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is relocated from his Washington, DC house to a military base due to threats against his life related to Operation Economic Outcast against the Iranian government.
The U.S. evacuates its military aircraft from RAF Mildenhall following a reported threat from Iran.
Nvidia launches an investigation into allegations that its CEO, Jensen Huang, was targeted by Chinese intelligence, following reports of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

CENTCOM expands its interdiction efforts against the Iranian government beyond its existing naval blockade by establishing Task Force Iron Gate to obstruct "illicit" shipments and weapons transit across land borders and the Caspian Sea.
The number of measles cases in the United States exceeds 5,000 for the first time since 1991.
Susie Wiles, Trump's White House Chief of Staff, is replaced by Stephen Miller, her deputy.
Eight Canadian money services companies are sanctioned by the U.S. for dealing with the Iranian government.
The US cuts off money exchanger MEXC due to transactions involving Iran, North Korea, and Russia.

Thomas Markle, the father of Megan, Duchess of Sussex, is detained in Lakeland, Florida, for allegedly possessing sex abuse photographs of preadolescent girls, including images depicting himself with them.
Trump declares that the US conducted "minor" strikes against Iran, targeting "a little bit of an anti-aircraft device."
The Central Command (CENTCOM) announces a $20 million incentive "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear program.
Harmeet Dhillon, the head of the Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division, resigns following the midterm elections.
A Venezuelan man is detained near the White House on suspicion of plotting to assassinate Trump.
First Lady Melania Trump receives the Order of Princess Olga from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for her significant personal contribution to humanitarian relief efforts in Ukraine.
The US imposes new sanctions on companies and individuals in India and Turkey with ties to the Iranian government.
Trump announces that the US will terminate all military aid to Israel, totaling $4 billion per year, by the end of 2026, but will continue to sell military hardware.
Small-scale, "defensive" strikes are carried out by the US against Iranian positions on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
A Washington state resident dies of bird flu.
Democratic senator Chris Murphy of Connecticut is hospitalized after suffering a stroke.
A Learjet 60 crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board.

Democratic representative Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic Abdul Al-Sayed in the Senate election in Michigan. Al-Sayed had previously defeated Stevens in the primaries. In response, Stevens's staff members resign and the Michigan Democratic Party revokes Stevens's party membership.

TRM Labs, an American blockchain analysis firm, reveals that North Korea's Bureau 121 was responsible for a $6.3 billion theft on cryptocurrency exchange Binance, the largest heist in history, prompting an investigation by the FBI and the US Secret Service.
The Trump administration authorizes the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fires Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the U.S. military's chief military planner.
QatarEnergy announces a long-term liquefied natural gas procurement agreement with the United States until 2054.
In an attempt to resume peace talks, Vice President JD Vance sends a letter to Iranian National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei at Trump's directive.
The District Court for the Eastern District of New York convicts a US woman of receiving Islamic State training after marrying an Islamic State militant at the age of 18.
The Milwaukee Brewers defeat the Tampa Bay Rays to win the 2026 World Series, their first championship in franchise history.
A grand jury declines to indict Cassidy Hutchinson over her January 6 testimony.
The White House announces that a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been agreed by President Putin and President Zelenskyy, mediated by First Lady Melania Trump.
President Trump confirms that Starlink service has been restored for Ukraine.
